headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0118 — A saved Slack connection is damaged and can't be used

html:
SMTO-SKL-0118 — A saved Slack connection is damaged and can't be used

GUID: 6d73219c-4aea-5173-80e7-d589447c2fcb
Slug: slack-workspace-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • The saved Slack workspace entry in Parameter Store has missing or wrong details, perhaps from being edited by hand, or its name belongs to a different kind of entry. SMTO didn't use it or contact Slack.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and find the Slack workspace entry named in your request. If you or someone else edited it by hand, change it back. These entries are written by SMTO when you connect, and hand edits easily break them.
  2. If you can't restore it, ask SMTO to connect Slack again with your Slack OAuth App entry, and give the new connection a name that isn't used yet. SMTO won't reuse a damaged entry's name, but a new name lets it save a fresh, correct entry.
  3. Once the new connection works, ask the person who manages SMTO to remove the damaged entry. Leaving it in place can cause the same message when a request points at it.

What success looks like

  • Your Slack request runs with the restored or newly connected workspace entry.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't copy access tokens out of the entry or paste them into a conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The slack_workspace record at the requested reference fails profile validation (wrong type or version, malformed IDs, inconsistent principal fields, missing access token while available, or a timezone-less expires_at), or the key holds a different profile type.

What this means

  • Workspace profile type, version or stored fields fail the supported schema. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Workspace profile type, version or stored fields fail the supported schema.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the supported profile fields and stored principal identity without inferring token type from its spelling.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the record against parameter_profiles.validate: profile_type slack_workspace, version 1, workspace_id T…, user_id U/W…, bot_user_id equal to user_id only for principal_type bot, access_token present when authorization_state is available, timezone-aware expires_at. Undo manual edits or restore it from backup; because slack.connect validates an existing workspace_key before reuse, otherwise connect with an explicit new, unused workspace_key (a default derived key that matches the damaged record is refused as workspace_changed) and remove the damaged record afterwards. Never infer the principal from a token prefix.
  • Reconnect the exact Slack workspace profile; do not infer token type from a token prefix.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported reconnection restores the intended valid workspace profile.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
